speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing your history. To better understand your progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger, could you please describe when the symptoms first started and if there was any specific injury or event that preceded them?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That sounds like a significant trauma. Did you hear a "pop" at the time of injury, and is there any visible deformity or bruising on the finger now?

REQUEST TEST: X_Ray_right_hand

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-ray of the Right Hand: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the swelling and pain continue to worsen despite rest and ice, or did it improve slightly? REQUEST TEST: MRI_right_ring_finger

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI of the Right Ring Finger: Preliminary findings indicate an intact extensor tendon and flexor tendons with no evidence of complete rupture. However, there is mild edema (fluid) surrounding the tendons at the level of the distal interphalangeal joint, consistent with the recent trauma and ongoing inflammation described by the patient.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Is the pain significantly worse with passive extension of the finger, and do you notice any difficulty straightening the tip of the ring finger compared to your other hand?

REQUEST TEST: Ultrasound_right_ring_finger

DIAGNOSIS READY: Extensor Digitorum Communis Tendonitis / Early Tenosynovitis

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
